title: Using So and Such
summary: Learn how to use 'so' and 'such' to make your English more expressive. You will practice describing people, places, and things with extra feeling.

sections.p: We use 'so' before an adjective to make it stronger. An adjective is a word that describes a noun, like 'cold', 'happy', or 'expensive'. You can use 'so' in everyday conversations to show how you really feel about something. For example, if the weather is very nice, you can say it is so warm outside today.

ex.mean: She is a very kind person.
This movie is not interesting at all.

sections.p: We use 'such' before a noun phrase that has an adjective and a noun together. If the noun is singular and countable, we use 'such a' or 'such an'. For plural nouns or uncountable nouns, we just use 'such' without 'a' or 'an'. It helps you describe things in a vivid and clear way.

ex.en: It is such a nice day.
ex.mean: It is a very good day.

sections.p: The main difference is what comes right after the word. Use 'so' when there is only an adjective. Use 'such' when there is a noun (with or without an adjective). Never put 'a' or 'an' after 'so', but always use 'a' or 'an' with singular countable nouns after 'such'.

ex.en: It was such a difficult test.

tip: Remember this simple rule: 'So' goes with an adjective alone, but 'Such' needs a noun to hold hands with!

quiz.en: We had ___ great time at the party.
